BETWEEN:-
 GANESH S/O RAMDAS GAUR, AGED ABOUT 34 YEARS,

OCCUPATION: SERVICE R/O: 17 GURUSHANKAR  NAGAR, DWARKAPURI DISTRICT INDORE (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI YOGESH GUPTA - ADVOCATE)

AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  STATION HOUSE OFFICER THROUGH POLICE STATION  - CRIME BRANCH, DIST. INDORE (MADHYA PRADESH)
 ....
 (BY SHRI SUHAS PUNDLIK - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)

This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER 1.

This is the 1st application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.32/2023 registered at Police Station - Crime Branch, Indore for the offence under Section 420, 409, 201 of IPC.

2. As per the prosecution story, complainant Dinesh Kumar has made a written complaint before the P.S. Crime Branch, Indore by stating that the applicant Ganesh who is the alleged officer posted in the Swastik Herbal Company, on the pretext of providing him more profit on herbal products, got deposited Rs.1,50,000/- in the company's Bank Account but after that he did not provide the herbal products to the complainant.
Accordingly offence has been registered.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is in custody since 19.6.2023.

Matter has been amicably settled between both the parties and complainant Dinesh Kumar has filed compromise application before Ganesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121844373/
1 the trial Court.

sentences.text: Complainant has also filed an affidavit that the matter has been amicably settled between both of them and the applicant has paid an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- to the complainant and he has no objection if bail is given to the present applicant.
Applicant is permanent resident of District Indore and doing business.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.

Hence,
he prays that applicant be released on bail.
4. Per-contra, learned GA for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.

5. Perused the case diary as well as the impugned order of the court below.
6.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, nature and gravity of allegation as also taking note of the fact that the matter has been amicably settled between both the parties and complainant himself has filed affidavit that the amount in question Rs.1,50,000/- has been paid by the applicant and no dispute remains between them, complainant has also pleaded No Objection regarding bail application of the applicant, in view of the above, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C.
C.C. as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE trilok Ganesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121844373/
